meta.title: Static Web Template - a JSON-driven static site engine
meta.description: A small, fast static site engine: one site-spec.json renders the whole page - no framework, no build step, no dependencies.
meta.author: Static Web Template

blocks.title: One JSON file. A whole website.
blocks.lead: This entire site - every tab, every block, the metadata, even this sentence - is rendered at runtime from a single site-spec.json. No framework, no build step, no dependencies.

blocks.text: You are looking at the engine documenting itself. Each tab is a section, and each section is an ordered list of typed blocks. Open Content blocks and Media blocks to see every block type the engine ships, then read How it works for the architecture behind it.

items.title: No build step
items.body: Plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS served as files. Clone it, edit the spec, deploy to any static host.

items.title: Config-driven blocks
items.body: Add a section or rearrange content by editing JSON. Adding a brand-new block type is a small, local code change.

items.title: Resilient by design
items.body: A broken or missing spec shows a calm error screen, never a blank page. A typo in one block never blanks the rest.

slides.title: The slideshow block
slides.caption: One slide is a framed image; two or more become a carousel.
slides.text: Arrows, dots, swipe gestures and a lightbox are all built in.

slides.caption: Every image on the site shares one lightbox overlay.
Hidden tabs' images are warmed in the background for instant switches.

blocks.name: The single source of truth
blocks.text: Everything the visitor sees lives in site-spec.json - the brand, the nav tabs, every section and block, the footer, the socials, the background images, and the document metadata. index.html is an almost-empty shell; engine.js fetches the spec on load and builds the page from it. To change what the site says, you edit the spec, not the markup.

blocks.name: The block engine
blocks.text: sections is an ordered array, and its order is both the nav order and the page order. Each section is a list of typed blocks, and rendering is one generic dispatch: the engine looks up each block's type in a renderer map and calls the matching builder. There is no per-section special-casing anywhere - which is exactly why adding a new kind of content stays a small change.

blocks.name: Resilient by design
blocks.text: Three failure modes - the spec fails to load, fails to parse, or has no usable sections - all land on the same calm temporarily unavailable screen with a contact escape hatch. The page never blanks and never throws. Unknown block types are skipped with a console warning, so one bad block can't take down the rest of the page.

blocks.name: Built for machines too
blocks.text: Because the page is JavaScript-rendered, the engine also mirrors the spec into formats a non-JS crawler can read: a plain-text llms.txt, a sitemap.xml, and a schema.org JSON-LD block - all stamped by generate-static.mjs so they can never drift from what visitors actually see. A dev-only launch-check.js validator refuses to let an inconsistent site ship.

items.q: Do I need Node or a build tool to run the site?
items.a: No. The deployed site is plain static files. Node is only used by the optional dev tools (generate-static and launch-check) - the live site never runs it.

items.q: Why does the page need a local web server?
items.a: The engine fetches site-spec.json, and browsers block that fetch over file://. Serve the folder with any static server, e.g. python3 -m http.server 8000, then open the localhost URL.

items.q: How do I add a brand-new kind of block?
items.a: Write a builder in engine.js and register it in the renderer map, add its CSS, document its shape, then add a validator rule and a schema entry. AGENTS.md walks through the full ripple so nothing drifts.

blocks.text: Everything below is a live block defined by a few lines of JSON. The small serif heading above most blocks is an optional name field.

blocks.title: A bold headline block.
blocks.lead: The hero renders an eyebrow, a large headline and a lead paragraph. The first hero on the page becomes the H1; later heroes are H2 with identical styling, so the page keeps a single H1 for SEO.

blocks.name: text
blocks.text: This paragraph is a text block. It renders prose with a small set of trusted inline tags - emphasis, strong, and links. Set format to markdown for a tiny markdown subset, or plain to escape everything. Every rich-text field is sanitized before it reaches the page.

blocks.name: cards
blocks.text: The cards block is a responsive grid. Cards can carry an optional meta line and, with linked set, become clickable.

items.title: Grid layout
items.body: Cards reflow from three columns down to one as the viewport narrows.

items.title: Optional link
items.body: Set linked: true and give an item a url to make the whole card a link.

items.title: Optional icon
items.body: An item icon adds a monochrome badge that auto-inverts in dark mode.

blocks.name: links
blocks.text: The links block renders contact rows - an icon, a label over the value, and an arrow cue. It's the same block that powers the Contact details below the fold.

blocks.name: table
blocks.blurb: The last column is styled as a price by default; set accentValue: false for prose tables like the one under How it works.

items.a: Yes. It uses native button toggles and is fully ARIA-wired and keyboard operable.
Reorder a section by reordering its blocks array - order in the JSON is order on the page.

blocks.text: Blocks that render images, embeds and structured data. All image blocks feed the same lightbox.

blocks.name: slideshow
blocks.blurb: One slide renders a framed image; two or more become a carousel with arrows, dots, swipe and a lightbox.

blocks.name: gallery
blocks.blurb: A paged, responsive image grid. Tap any tile to open the shared lightbox.

blocks.name: photo
blocks.text: The photo block is single-image sugar - it normalizes to a one-image gallery, so a lone picture still gets the frame and lightbox.

blocks.name: map
blocks.text: The map block embeds a live map, or with mode: static renders a clean themed address card instead. Hidden tabs' embeds are warmed in the background so the tab opens instantly.

blocks.name: hours
blocks.blurb: Reads the opening times from business.hours and highlights the current day.

blocks.name: review
blocks.blurb: Outbound call-to-action buttons that send visitors to review platforms - links only, no backend.

blocks.name: video
blocks.text: The video block embeds a privacy-enhanced, lazy-loaded YouTube player. Point it at one video, or at a channel's uploads playlist to always show the newest.
Getting your own site live takes about five minutes.

items.title: Edit the spec
items.body: Open site-spec.json and change the brand, tabs, blocks and contact details.

items.title: Add your images
items.body: Drop backgrounds and photos into the assets folder and point the spec at them.

items.title: Refresh the mirrors
items.body: Run node generate-static.mjs to rebuild llms.txt, the sitemap and the JSON-LD.

items.title: Run the gate
items.body: Run node launch-check.js and fix every error it reports - stray demo text, fake contact data, broken assets.

items.title: Deploy
items.body: Push the folder to GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages or any static host.

blocks.name: Theming
blocks.text: Colors live as CSS custom properties in styles.css, grouped under a dark and a light block; changing those variables re-skins the whole site, including the 404 page and the browser chrome color. Dark is the default. Fonts (Inter and Oswald) are self-hosted, so there's no Google Fonts request - and a site can override brand tokens per-client via an optional theme object in the spec.

blocks.name: Where to go next
blocks.text: Read README.md for the human quick-start, AGENTS.md for the architecture and how to add a block type, and CLIENT-CHECKLIST.md for the per-client fill-in list. This demo was built from m-remis/static-web-template.

blocks.text: The same links block, laid out as tiles with brand-tinted icons - here pointing at social platforms instead of contact methods. The header and mobile drawer render these same platforms from the socials list.
